name: MRKL Systems (Modular Reasoning, Knowledge and Language)
executive_summary: A foundational architecture predating ReAct and most agent frameworks: route a query to the right combination of an LLM and external 'expert modules' instead of one model doing it all.
description: Positioned as a discussion/position paper rather than a single benchmarked technique, MRKL argues that expecting a single LLM to internalize all knowledge and all computational ability (e.g. exact arithmetic) is the wrong architecture — instead, treat the LLM as a router/orchestrator among a set of external 'expert' modules (which can themselves be neural or symbolic, e.g. a calculator, a database query engine, another fine-tuned model), extensible by adding new experts over time. Frequently cited as an early conceptual ancestor of the entire modern LLM-agent-with-tools paradigm (ReAct, ART, ReWOO, and the many agent frameworks built since) — most of this catalog's `agentic-tool-use` category can trace its lineage back to this proposal's core framing.
when_to_use: Conceptual grounding for why routing to specialized external modules (rather than relying on one model for everything) is the right architecture — useful when explaining or justifying an agent-with-tools design to a stakeholder.
Designing a system meant to be extensible with new expert modules over time, since extensibility is a first-class concern in the original proposal.
when_not_to_use: N/A for direct application — this is an architectural position/framework paper rather than a specific technique with a single benchmarked prompting recipe; the later, more specific techniques it inspired (ReAct, ART, ReWOO) are more directly applicable starting points.
known_pitfalls: Being a foundational/conceptual proposal rather than a specific benchmarked method, it doesn't itself specify exact prompting mechanics — later papers (ReAct, ART) fill in the concrete implementation details.

primary_source.authors: Karpas, Abend, Belinkov, Lenz, Lieber, Ratner, Shoham, Bata, Levine, Leyton-Brown, et al.
primary_source.title: MRKL Systems: A Modular, Neuro-Symbolic Architecture that Combines Large Language Models, External Knowledge Sources and Discrete Reasoning
